chunks.heading: Who is eligible
chunks.text: Medicaid members who have no other way to get to a covered medical appointment can use non-emergency medical transportation at no cost. This includes rides to dialysis, behavioral health visits, pharmacy pickups after a visit and other covered services.
chunks.embedText: Non-Emergency Medical Transportation (NEMT) | Who is eligible | Medicaid members who have no other way to get to a covered medical appointment can use non-emergency medical transportation at no cost. This includes rides to dialysis, behavioral health visits, pharmacy pickups after a visit and other covered services.

chunks.heading: Scheduling a ride
chunks.text: Rides must be scheduled at least 2 business days before the appointment through the transportation vendor line. Same-day rides are allowed for hospital discharges and urgent appointments. Standing orders can be set up for recurring treatments such as dialysis or chemotherapy.

chunks.heading: Mileage reimbursement
chunks.text: Members who drive themselves or get a ride from a friend or family member can be reimbursed for mileage at the state rate. The member must submit a trip log signed by the provider office within 90 days of the appointment.

chunks.heading: Complaints and no-shows
chunks.text: If the driver did not arrive or the member was late to an appointment, log a complaint in CRM with category Transportation. The transportation vendor must respond within 24 hours. Repeated no-shows are escalated to the vendor manager.
